Verified. The bead asked to confirm the last fetch round is consulted ('may already be fixed by the final-try logic'), and it is — but nothing had ever demonstrated it.

Its original, PKIX-q9hv.1, was closed on 2026-06-04 with 'Added final build_first_valid_path call after AIA loop'. This re-filing was created on 2026-06-15, after that fix, precisely as a verification task. Nothing in the suite exercised the boundary: the only max_depth test sets it to 0, which confirms the degenerate case and says nothing about where the cap falls. So the fix was asserted and not demonstrated for five months.

It works, and the boundary is exactly where the constant claims. Traced the loop: with max_depth = 5, fetch rounds happen at iterations 0 through 4 (five rounds), then iteration 5 trips the cap branch and makes one more build attempt against the fully-augmented pool. Five rounds, six build attempts, last fetch consulted.

Demonstrated with new fixtures: deep-leaf.der needs five sequential fetches, since every intermediate is discoverable only from the caIssuers URI of the certificate below it. It validates under the default cap, consumes exactly five fetches, and Deep I5 — which arrives only in the final round — is present in the result. That is the assertion that distinguishes 'used' from 'paid for'.

Three tests, not one: four rounds must fail (otherwise the first test might be measuring a chain that always fit), and a sweep over caps 3/4/5/6 pins the boundary in both directions, so neither removing the final attempt nor allowing an extra round can pass unnoticed. Verified by deleting the final-attempt logic and confirming exactly those tests fail.

Also rewrote AIA_MAX_DEPTH's documentation, which was the other half of the original bead ('the rustdoc would then mean 5 hops resolved rather than 4'): it now states that the number counts hops resolved, that a cap of N resolves a chain needing N fetches and fails one needing N+1, and gives the real reason five is generous instead of citing a bead ID.

2325 workspace tests green; fmt, clippy, rustdoc, typos and the --depth 2 powerset all clean under RUSTFLAGS and RUSTDOCFLAGS both -D warnings. Commit 4ad34968.
